|# The Taste of Luxury : Bernard Arnault and the Moet-Hennessy Louis Vuitton Story
Front Cover
Jane Charlton , Nadege Forestier , Nazanine Ravai
DIANE Publishing Company , 1999 - Biography & Autobiography - 203 pages
* The story of the fierce battle for control of the world's leading luxury goods company, & of how Bernard Arnault, the son of a provincial French businessman, became head of LVMH Moet-Hennessy Louis Vuitton, controlling companies such as Givenchy, Dior, Moet & Christian Lacroix. He determined to merge Dior with the most glamorous names in luxury goods. He established a secret alliance with Guinness & assembled the world's largest luxury goods conglomerate. This is also the story of Arnault's bitter fight with his chief rival, Henry Racamier, with both men determined not to lose control of their business empires.

Arnault's Early Years and the Acquisition of Boussac

In The Taste of Luxury , Nadege Forestier and Nazanine Ravai start by describing Bernard Arnault's early career in his family's construction business. Not content with his position, Arnault always harbored ambitions of becoming a titan of a more glamorous industry.
The opportunity presented itself when the Boussac empire, which included the prestigious fashion house Christian Dior, went up for sale. Arnault acquired the beleaguered company at a bargain price, seizing the opportunity to enter the lucrative and glamorous world of fashion.

Arnault's Takeover of LVMH

Next, we move on to witness Arnault's aggressive takeover of the luxury goods conglomerate LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton, commonly known as LVMH. The authors describe his tenacious and strategic moves in accumulating shares and leveraging alliances, eventually gaining control of the board. “He was always the first in everything,” says Nadège Forestier, a journalist for Le Figaro , who worked with him regularly during the years of his rise.
